comment: Menu label for Traditional Chinese; shown in its own endonym across all languages.
Menu label for Hong Kong Traditional Chinese; shown in its own endonym across all languages.
Recording Rules manager button that opens the rule editor for the selected rule.
Title bar of the rule editor when creating a new rule.
Title bar of the rule editor when editing an existing rule.
Rule editor field label: how the title is matched (Exact / Contains).
Rule editor field label: start recording this many minutes early.
Rule editor field label: keep recording this many minutes late.
Unit shown after the lead/trail padding number fields (minutes).

Meters dialog slider caption, shown INSTEAD of 'Smooth' when the row's look is VU. Same MeterTuning field (smoothing); on an analog needle it is mechanical damping, not attack/decay easing. Keep it short - the caption sits over a narrow slider.
Caption above the Data-flow meter's single colour swatch, which sets the liquid's colour. Short - it sits over a narrow swatch column.
Button opening the author's Buy Me a Coffee tip page. Used in the About box and the support prompt.

Button opening the author's Ko-fi tip page (a second tip backend, so a user who can't or won't use Buy Me a Coffee's card checkout has a PayPal-capable alternative). 'Ko-fi' is a BRAND NAME — do not translate it; translate only any surrounding words.
Settings ▸ Channels: reset every channel's dead-link result back to 'not checked'. The undo for a dead-link sweep.
Confirmation before clearing dead-link results. Must make clear that a fresh sweep is needed to get them back.
Confirms cleared dead-link results. {0} = number of channels reset.
Shown when clearing dead-link results failed to write (e.g. the DB was locked). Must NOT read as success - the channels are still marked.
PIP right-click menu: promote the picture-in-picture's channel to the main view and demote the main view's channel into the PIP.
PIP right-click menu: close the picture-in-picture (returns to single view). Says 'close', not 'single view', because that is what the user is doing from inside the PIP.
Confirms a completed PIP<->main swap.
Heading of the About box's tip section, above the two tip buttons. Short — it is a section label, not a sentence.

Explains what the two tip buttons do, so they don't read as a purchase. Must NOT describe how the two backends differ (which payment methods each accepts depends on the creator's settings and would go stale). KEEP IT TO 2 LINES at the About box's width — a third line eats the headroom above the button row and starts crowding the disclaimer above.
Title of the one-time 'support this project' prompt.
Headline of the support prompt.
Body of the support prompt. Keep it warm and low-pressure; it must make clear the user will not be nagged.
Defers the support prompt; it reappears after a week.
Dismisses the support prompt permanently — it is never shown again.
Splash tagline. Tin foil on the aerial tips is the classic rabbit-ears reception remedy — translate the gag, not the words.
Settings menu item opening the System settings dialog.
Section header above the log-level control.
Explains that more detail helps when reporting a problem, and where the file lives.
Button revealing the log file in Explorer.
Section header above the beta feature toggles.
Warns that beta features are unfinished and off by default.
Log level name.
Log level name.
Log level name (the default).
Log level name.
Log level name (most verbose).
Checkable View-menu item: keep the PIP window above other applications.
Label for the global 'glass cover' strength slider in the Meters dialog.
Shown beside the glass slider when its strength is zero.
Schedule list status: this airing was skipped; its series rule is still active.
Status line after skipping one airing of a series rule.
Meter look: classic analog VU needle gauge. 'VU' is the standard audio abbreviation (volume unit) — keep it as VU.
Channels menu item: start the beta dead-link sweep.
Same item while a sweep is already running (greyed).
{0} = probes done, {1} = total.
{0} = channels found dead, {1} = rows updated.
Shown when the sweep was discarded (network problem) or cancelled.
The VOD root in the sidebar. Present only when the library contains movies.
Selecting the Movies root shows no grid — a VOD library is tens of thousands of items.
Settings > Channels. Only appears when an Xtream provider playlist exists.
Same menu item while a sync is running (greyed).
First phase: the account/auth probe.
Second phase: downloading the categories + the movie list (tens of MB).
{0} = number of movies being written to the database.
{0} = rows added or updated, {1} = rows removed because the provider dropped them.
{0} = rows added or updated, {1} = rows removed, {2} = unusable items. Shown when the trust guard refused the deletion pass on at least one playlist.
The provider answered, but with no usable movies. Nothing is written.
Refusal: Xtream lines commonly allow only one connection, so a sync during playback kicks the stream.
Refusal: no playlist URL carries Xtream credentials.
The sync was stopped (app closing) before anything was written.
{0} = a short technical reason (HTTP/JSON), not localized.
A run that committed work and then stopped. {0} = rows added or updated, {1} = the technical reason it stopped.
Appended to whatever the status line says when the grid was capped. {0} = the cap (5000). Leading separator included.
